reasons: The rule expressly treats the absence of any Customer convenience right in a multi-year term as walk-away territory; the cited text shows a three-year take-or-pay commitment (2.1) and only for-cause / insolvency / security-based termination rights (9.1-9.3), with no convenience right, so 'missing' is the correct classification and neither the preferred nor the fallback position is met.

The inserted language tracks the model clause closely (30 days' written notice, refund of prepaid Fees for the post-termination period, no Vendor convenience right) and adds a targeted 'Notwithstanding Section 2.1' carve-out so the new right is not swallowed by the take-or-pay lock-in — an actionable, minimally invasive insertion placed logically between 9.3 and 9.5 rather than a rewrite of existing text.

No existing Vendor convenience right appears in the record, so the absence of a deletion is consistent; the edit does not duplicate the separate take-or-pay commercial term beyond the override needed to make the exit effective.
Comment is accurate, concise, first-person plural, states what changed and why, and offers the 60-day fallback as permitted by the playbook.

Minor nit only: the rationale describes the insertion as 'a new Section 9.4' but the rendered paragraph carries no number, so the clause should be labelled 9.4 for consistency with the surrounding numbering; this does not affect substance or enforceability of the proposal.
